column3: A lake ringed by hills, causeways, willows and pagodas, loved by poets for over a thousand years. Su Dongpo and Bai Juyi each built a causeway here. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the heart of Hangzhou.
A Buddhist temple founded in the fourth century, tucked into a wooded hill, with thousands of stone carvings along the cliff nearby. It is one of the oldest and most visited temples in China.
A pagoda on the lakeshore, built again in 2002, tied to the legend of the White Snake. Its sunset view over West Lake is a famous one.
A small stone bridge on West Lake where, in the White Snake legend, the lovers met in the rain. In winter, a dusting of snow on the arch gives the bridge its name.
A wetland of waterways, reeds and persimmon trees inside the city, which you explore by boat. A quiet escape from the crowds.
A village among hills of tea bushes, where Dragon Well tea is grown. Visitors can taste fresh tea in the farmers' homes.
A pagoda of thirteen outside levels beside the Qiantang River, built in the tenth century to calm the river's tidal bore.
A restored old street with shops, teahouses and snack stalls, lit by lanterns in the evening.
A whole fish poached and covered with a glossy sweet-and-sour sauce. A classic of Hangzhou cooking, and sometimes an acquired taste.
Squares of pork belly braised slowly in soy sauce and rice wine until they melt in the mouth. Named for the poet Su Dongpo, who is said to have created the dish while governor of Hangzhou.
River shrimp stir-fried with fresh Dragon Well tea leaves, a light and fragrant dish, subtle in color and taste.
Chicken stuffed with herbs, wrapped in lotus leaves and clay, and baked. You crack the clay open at the table. Legend says a beggar invented it.
A bowl of noodles with sliced pork, bamboo shoots and pickled greens, a favorite breakfast in Hangzhou.
A flat green tea, pan-fried by hand, with a fresh, nutty taste. It is grown around West Lake and is among the best-known teas in China. Fresh spring leaves are the most prized.
A gentle, lyrical opera that began in Zhejiang, traditionally sung entirely by women, famous for love stories like Butterfly Lovers.
A library built in the 1500s, one of the oldest private libraries in Asia, which survived fires thanks to its design with water around it.
A riverside stretch of old European-style buildings, once a trading port, now with cafés and bars.
A large Chan Buddhist temple deep in a forest, where Japanese monks once came to study.
A site of a neolithic village about 7,000 years old, where rice, boats and wooden houses on stilts were found.
Rice balls filled with black sesame and lard, boiled and served in sweet soup. A famous Ningbo dessert, eaten at festivals.
Chewy rice cake, stir-fried with vegetables or pork, or boiled in soup, a staple of Ningbo.
Raw crab pickled in brine, served with rice, a strong coastal taste for the brave.
The old home of the writer Lu Xun and the streets from his stories, with a school, a garden and a tavern. It gives a feel for the water town of the early 1900s.
A garden where, in 353, Wang Xizhi and his friends wrote poems over wine and he wrote a famous piece of calligraphy.
Small boats with a black bamboo canopy, rowed by hand, that carry visitors through the canals.
A rice wine aged in clay jars, amber in color, used in cooking and drunk warm. The best-known drink of Shaoxing, and the base of many Zhejiang dishes.
Dried broad beans simmered with fennel, a snack with wine, famous from a Lu Xun story.
Pork belly steamed over salty dried greens until rich and soft, a hearty home dish.
Tofu that is fermented until it smells strong, then fried. It is crisp outside, soft inside, and loved by many.
A mountain of strange peaks, waterfalls and caves, with the cliffs lit at night in a show of light.
An island in the river with two pagodas, a poet's retreat since the Tang dynasty.
A clear river winding through old villages and hills, perfect for rafting.
Springy fish balls in a clear soup, a Wenzhou breakfast snack.
A sweet, fragrant tangerine with a thin skin, once a tribute to the emperor.
A lake where a founding meeting of the Communist Party was concluded on a boat in 1921. A replica boat is on display.
A canal town with stilt houses, stone bridges, waterside teahouses and a theater. It looks beautiful in the evening with lights on the water, and hosts a World Internet Conference.
A water town known for its covered walkways along the canals, so you can walk in the rain.
Sticky rice dumplings wrapped in bamboo leaves, with a fatty pork or sweet bean filling. Jiaxing is the most famous place for them.
A water plant with a sweet, crisp taste, harvested from the lake in autumn.
A mountain covered in bamboo, with old villas and cool summer air, a retreat for Shanghai residents.
A silk-trading town where wealthy merchants built grand houses, with a mix of Chinese and European styles.
Writing brushes made in Huzhou for 700 years, loved by calligraphers, made of goat or weasel hair.
Tiny, transparent fish from Lake Tai, often scrambled with egg or in soup.
The world's biggest wholesale market for small goods, from toys to Christmas decorations, with hundreds of thousands of products.
A giant film studio with copies of the Forbidden City, a Qing street and old Hong Kong, where many Chinese films and dramas are shot.
A dry-cured ham with a deep red color and rich taste, aged for a year or more. It flavors soups and stir-fries.
A Buddhist mountain, the birthplace of the Tiantai school, with temples among cliffs and waterfalls.
Fresh crabs, shrimps and fish from the East China Sea, usually steamed or braised.
An island sacred to Guanyin, the bodhisattva of compassion, with temples, sea views and sandy beaches. Pilgrims come by ferry to burn incense and pray.
An island with long sandy beaches, popular with summer visitors.
Yellow croaker, crab, shrimp and shellfish from the fishing grounds around Zhoushan.
A long silver fish, fried or braised, which is a favorite of the Zhejiang coast.
Celadon pottery with a soft green glaze, made here for around 1,700 years, once exported worldwide.
A braised duck head snack, spicy and rich, popular in Quzhou.
